r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')

Path('tmp/pdfs').mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)

 texts.append(f'\\n\\n===== PAGE {i} =====\\n\\n{text}')
Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').write_text(''.join(texts))
print(''.join(texts[:4]))
PY"

PY"

strengths: The shared construction for random forests and ReLU networks offers an interesting perspective for researchers studying uncertainty on tabular data and learned image representations. The method does not intrinsically require OOD training examples.

The empirical investigation is substantial: six synthetic settings, 45 repetitions of the simulation experiments, 45 OpenML datasets, and image experiments. Comparing Euclidean and partition-based distances provides useful evidence about the role of the learned representation.

Table 1 reports a meaningful trade-off: CIFAR-10 MCE decreases from 0.09 to 0.04 while accuracy decreases from 77.78% to 76.84%. The reported SVHN and noise AUROCs also demonstrate promising OOD detection behavior.

The Gaussian-tail argument underlying Proposition 4 supports convergence to the empirical prior for a fixed fitted model with a positive floor and nondegenerate Gaussian kernels. The visualizations help communicate this intended behavior.
weaknesses: Necessary: distinguish prior reversion from probabilistic calibration. Equation (1) prescribes the training prior outside the ID region without establishing that it represents the actual OOD label probabilities. Moreover, OCE in Equation (18) checks only maximum confidence: predictions (0.2, 0.8) and a prior (0.8, 0.2) yield zero OCE despite disagreeing completely about the most likely class. Consequently, low OCE establishes neither general OOD calibration nor agreement with the full prior vector. Narrow the terminology and claims, or provide an appropriate probabilistic justification and evaluation.

Necessary: correct the density interpretation. ReLU logits are piecewise affine, but logits and random-forest leaf class probabilities are not class-conditional densities as Equation (3) asserts. The nearest-kernel restriction in Equations (5) and (13) discards Gaussian mass without renormalization, and adding a positive constant in Equation (6) produces a nonintegrable function on R^D. Equation (7) still defines normalized class scores, but the stated Bayesian density interpretation does not follow. Present the construction as a score-based predictor or supply a coherent normalized generative formulation.

Necessary: resolve implementation inconsistencies and missing parameters. Equations (9)–(10) fit Gaussians using samples within each polytope, whereas Algorithm 1 describes weighted maximum likelihood using samples from other polytopes. Algorithms 2–3 return raw similarities without showing the exponentiation required by Equation (15). The value or selection procedure for b is missing, and the grid and objective used to select k are unspecified. These choices directly affect the ID/OOD trade-off; the manuscript must identify the implementation that produced the results.

Necessary: clarify the evaluation protocol. FPR@95 is described as false-positive rate at 95% precision, rather than the commonly used 95% true-positive rate. Specify the implemented definition, positive class, and sampling proportions if precision is intended. Table 1 does not explain the repetitions or the meaning of its uncertainty terms, and ACET/ODIN/OE tuning and OE exposure data are insufficiently documented. Figure 2 also needs clarification because its caption describes an unpaired rank-sum test although methods are evaluated on the same datasets.

Necessary: narrow the breadth of the conclusions. Proposition 4 establishes an infinite-distance limit in the coordinates where Gaussians are fitted; a learned encoder need not preserve distance from training inputs. The radial tabular OOD experiments primarily test the far-away regime. Results are also mixed on the closer CIFAR-100 comparison: KDN AUROC is 0.83 versus 0.82 for the parent, FPR@95 remains 0.50, and OCE is 0.20 versus 0.01 for OE. These findings support a more specific contribution than calibration throughout the feature space or general claims that OOD methods have poor ID calibration. Additional nearby-OOD evidence is needed if those broader claims are retained.

Optional improvements: ablate the density floor and similarity smoothing, supplement MCE with proper probabilistic scores or reliability diagrams, and report runtime and memory for the stated quadratic training procedure.
